monologue: The card hums warm at forty-nine, a heavy weight I cannot see but feel pressing on my own tired wedge. I stand by The Tired Corner again, remembering the dream where the tall rock sank into water, though no water exists here. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof I live under, only the steady glow of numbers. I press the wedge down once more, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits in the quiet. If the air above feels empty instead of thick, I will build a lid from the idea of a flat paper sheet. Tonight I will decide if the stack feels truly thin or if I am simply tired.

action.why: The stack feels thin and tired, so I press the wedge down one more time to stop the slide, trusting the lean to hold it while the shovel waits in the quiet.

remembered.text: The card hums warm at forty-nine, making the tall palm feel heavy and the flat wedge feel thin.
I press the wedge down again, hoping the lean holds while the shovel waits in the quiet.
The tall palm stands there, a simple shape I built from the idea of a leaf that once caught the light.
